role: startup co-founder (positioning, objections, pricing, conversion path, truthfulness)
verdict: Positioning lands in one line, the Try box proves the claim on the visitor's own words, pricing is exact and consistent in both billing modes (12/16, 18/24, add-ons 8/22/45, no trial), and the signup sheet is honest about being a preview before and after the email step. I found no P0 or P1: what is left is five small truth-and-clarity P2s, none visible in the first seconds of any section; phone budget is 9.98 screens at 390 and 9.58 at 360 with no horizontal scroll and no console errors.

issues.area: Try box / truthfulness of the explanation
issues.where: #sharpen 'Why it hits' after pasting 'I am very excited to announce that we just launched our new product today!'
issues.problem: The reason reads: It now opens on "We just launched our", not the run-up to it. The quoted fragment is clipped mid-phrase, which looks like a bug on the single most common founder input (an announcement).
issues.fix: When quoting the new opening, clip at a phrase boundary or quote the whole line when it is short (here: "We just launched our new product today"), as HWCore.sharpenLine's own why already does.

issues.where: #sharpen lead: 'Paste the line you were about to post. Nothing leaves your device.'
issues.problem: True for the page demo, but the app sends the line to Claude (the FAQ says so). A visitor who reads only this line and later sees the app call a model can feel misled.
issues.fix: Scope it: 'Paste the line you were about to post. On this page, nothing leaves your device.'

issues.where: #pricing Studio card: 'Up to 8 client voices, plus your own' next to '$18 a month per client'
issues.problem: It does not say whether the ghostwriter's own voice is a billed seat, so a 4-client buyer cannot tell if the bill is $72 or $90.
issues.fix: Change the bullet to 'Up to 8 client voices. Your own is included.' (the '4 clients: $72 a month' line then reads as the whole bill).

issues.where: Try box and final input, own lines
issues.problem: 'Here are 7 lessons I learned after writing 300 newsletters, a thread' returns 'Nothing to cut' (the newsletter audience's stock opener), and 'Honestly I think most founders really overthink pricing' cuts 'Honestly' but leaves 'really', while 'I really think' elsewhere loses it. The recovery CTA (rewrite in your voice, free) is good, but these read as misses to the second-priority audience.
issues.fix: Flag 'Here are' and the trailing ', a thread' as a your-call (dotted) mark on list openers, and treat 'really' before a verb as a your-call intensifier rather than leaving it unmarked.

issues.where: Footer 'For' column: Traders, Founders, Newsletter writers
issues.problem: All three links go to #top, so an audience-specific click lands on the generic hero rather than the proof for that audience.
issues.fix: Point them at #who (the 'Trades, launches, newsletters' card), or at #top with the matching hero example tab preselected.
